## plot function prototypes
### hist_for_single_rate_version()
```{r}
#| label: hist_for_single_rate_version() prototype
hist_for_single_rate_version <- function(
  annual_change_table,
  version_elec,
  x_limits = c(-3000, 3000),
  y_limits = c(0, 1000),
  binwidth = 100,
  show_category_labels = TRUE
) {

  # --------------------------------------
  # Plot parameters
  x_min <- x_limits[1]
  x_max <- x_limits[2]

  # Define the breaks for binning
  breaks <- seq(floor(x_min/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(x_max/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)

  # More balanced color palette with less contrast
  dark_red <- "#db8b87"        # dark red
  light_red <- "#eaada9"       # light red
  light_green <- "#8ebd85"     # light green
  dark_green <- "#5e8a5e"      # dark green
  # --------------------------------------

  # Filter data for mid_hp
  plot_data <- annual_change_table |>
    filter(hvac == "mid_hp", version_elec == !!version_elec) |>
    # Add category column before binning with new cutoffs
    mutate(bill_category = case_when(
      annual_bill_change <= -1000 ~ "large_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 0 ~ "small_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 1000 ~ "small_increase",
      TRUE ~ "large_increase"
    ))

  # Calculate percentages for each category
  category_percentages <- plot_data |>
    group_by(bill_category) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(percentage = count / sum(count) * 100)

  # Get percentages for annotation
  pct_large_savings <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "large_savings") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_large_savings) == 0) pct_large_savings <- 0

  pct_small_savings <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "small_savings") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_small_savings) == 0) pct_small_savings <- 0

  pct_small_increase <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "small_increase") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_small_increase) == 0) pct_small_increase <- 0

  pct_large_increase <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "large_increase") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_large_increase) == 0) pct_large_increase <- 0

  # Manually bin the data and calculate counts - this preserves the bill_category
  binned_data <- plot_data |>
    mutate(bin = cut(annual_bill_change,
                     breaks = breaks,
                     include.lowest = TRUE,
                     right = FALSE)) |>
    group_by(bin, bill_category) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    # Add bin midpoint for plotting
    mutate(bin_mid = as.numeric(as.character(
      sapply(bin, function(b) {
        # Extract bin boundaries and calculate midpoint
        vals <- as.numeric(gsub("\\(|\\]|\\[|\\)", "", strsplit(as.character(b), ",")[[1]]))
        return(mean(vals))
      })
    )))

  # Position the bars at the very top and text just below
  bar_y_pos <- y_limits[2]  # Exactly at the top
  text_y_pos <- y_limits[2] * 0.95  # Just below the colored line

  # Calculate x positions for percentage labels (center of each category)
  x_large_savings <- mean(c(x_min, -1000))
  x_small_savings <- mean(c(-1000, 0))
  x_small_increase <- mean(c(0, 1000))
  x_large_increase <- mean(c(1000, x_max))

  # Create the plot using geom_col() with binned data
  px_hist_by_rate_version <- ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = bin_mid, y = count, fill = bill_category)) +
    # Add vertical dotted lines at the category boundaries
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1000, 0, 1000), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", size = 0.5) +

    # Add the bars
    geom_col(position = "stack", width = binwidth * 0.9) +

    # Set the fill colors manually with expanded categories
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "large_savings" = "#5e8a5e",      # dark green
        "small_savings" = "#8ebd85",      # light green
        "small_increase" = "#eaada9",     # light red
        "large_increase" = "#db8b87"      # dark red
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +

    # Add horizontal lines at the very top of the plot
    # With colors matching their respective categories
    annotate("segment",
             x = x_min, xend = -1000,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = dark_green, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = -1000, xend = 0,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = light_green, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = 0, xend = 1000,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = light_red, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = 1000, xend = x_max,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = dark_red, size = 1) +

    # Add percentage labels for each category directly below the lines
    annotate("text",
             x = x_large_savings,
             y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
             label = paste0(pct_large_savings, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_small_savings,
             y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
             label = paste0(pct_small_savings, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_small_increase,
             y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
             label = paste0(pct_small_increase, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_large_increase,
             y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
             label = paste0(pct_large_increase, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    # Rest of the plot styling
    labs(
      title = glue::glue("Change in Total Winter Energy Bills after Switching to Heat Pumps"),
      x = "Annual Bill Change ($)",
      y = "# of Homes"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 242.13 * 0.001), "k"),
      name = "# of Homes",
      limits = y_limits,
      breaks = seq(0, y_limits[2]*242.13, by=50000)/242.13
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::dollar_format(),
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, by = 500)
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      aspect.ratio = 0.6
    ) +
    {
      if (show_category_labels) {
        list(
          annotate("text", x = x_large_savings,   y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "savings > $1k",  size = 3, fontface = "bold"),
          annotate("text", x = x_small_savings,   y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "savings $0–1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold"),  # make bold
          annotate("text", x = x_small_increase,  y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "losses  $0–1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold"),  # make bold
          annotate("text", x = x_large_increase,  y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "losses  > $1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold")
        )
      }
    } +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

  return(list(px_hist_by_rate_version, category_percentages))
}

```

### plot_bill_change_histograms()
```{r}
#| label: plot_bill_change_histograms() prototype

plot_bill_change_histograms <- function(
  annual_change_table,
  bill_type,
  baseline_heating_type_option,
  electric_utility_option,
  supply_year,
  second_subtitle = NULL,
  x_limits = c(-2500, 2500),
  y_limits = c(0, 100000)/242.13,
  binwidth = 100
) {


  # Create nicer version labels
  version_labels <- c(
    "baseline" = "Default Rates",
    "hpr_approved" = "1.0 Rates",
    "hpr_doer" = "2.0 Rates"
  )

  # Create three histograms without individual titles
  result_baseline <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    version_elec = "baseline",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p1_baseline <- result_baseline[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +                 # Remove y-axis label
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x axis title from top two plots
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x tick labels from top two plots
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x ticks from top two plots
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 0, 5),  # Consistent margins (top, right, bottom, left)
      axis.title.y = element_blank()     # Remove y title from top plot
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["baseline"],
             hjust = 1,
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "#023047")

  result_approved <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    version_elec = "hpr_approved",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p2_approved <- result_approved[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x axis title from top two plots
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x tick labels from top two plots
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x ticks from top two plots
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),   # Remove y title from middle plot
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 0, 5)  # Consistent margins (no top/bottom margin)
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["hpr_approved"],
             hjust = 1,
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "#FC9706")

  result_doer <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    version_elec = "hpr_doer",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p3_doer <- result_doer[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +
    theme(
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),  # Remove y title from bottom plot
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 5, 5),  # Consistent margins
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["hpr_doer"],
             hjust = 1,
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "#68BED8")

  # print(result_baseline[[1]])
  # print(result_approved[[1]])
  # print(result_doer[[1]])

  # Combine plots with shared x and y axes
  combined_plot <- p1_baseline / p2_approved / p3_doer +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1)) +  # Equal heights for all plots
    plot_annotation(
      title = case_when(
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_elec" ~ glue::glue("Switching from {baseline_heating_type_option} to Heat Pump: Change in Annual Electric Bill"),
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_energy" ~ glue::glue("Change in Total Winter Energy Bills after Switching to Heat Pump from {baseline_heating_type_option}"),
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_gas" ~ glue::glue("Switching from {baseline_heating_type_option} to Heat Pump: Change in Annual Gas Bill"),
        TRUE ~ "Heat Pump Rate Bill Changes" # Default case
      ),
      subtitle = second_subtitle,
      theme = theme(
        plot.margin = margin(10, 25, 10, 10),  # Add more right margin for labels
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
      )
    ) &
    # Apply consistent theming to all plots
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      aspect.ratio = 0.18,
    )

  # Wrap the combined plot to add a shared y-axis label
  combined_plot <- patchwork::wrap_elements(combined_plot) +
    labs(tag = "# of Homes") +
    theme(
      plot.tag = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, face = "plain", size = 9),
      plot.tag.position = "left"
    )

  return(list(combined_plot, result_baseline[[2]], result_approved[[2]], result_doer[[2]]))
}


```

## fig-stacked-bar-components-delivery-on-top
```{r}
#| label: fig-stacked-bar-components-delivery-on-top
#| fig-cap: "Median electric bill for Massachusetts homes that install air-source heat pumps, under default, 1.0 and 2.0 heat pump rates."

bill_component_colors = c(
  "annual_gas_bill" = "grey50", # grey
  "annual_elec_supply_charge" = "#A0AF12",
  "annual_elec_delivery_charge" = "#023047",
  "annual_elec_customer_charge" = "#68BED8",
  "pre_hp_delivery_total" = "#FC9706"
)


stack_order_delivery_on_top = c(
  "annual_gas_bill",
  "annual_elec_delivery_charge", # top
  "annual_elec_customer_charge", # middle
  "annual_elec_supply_charge" # bottom
)

components <- factor(stack_order_delivery_on_top, levels = stack_order_delivery_on_top)

annual_bills_by_component_plot <- annual_bills_by_component |>
  arrange(match(charge_type, components)) |>
  filter(hvac == "mid_hp")


# Ugly, but here we get the balues from the stacked bar chart
y_baseline_customer_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "baseline", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_customer_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_baseline_delivery_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "baseline", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_delivery_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_baseline_supply_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "baseline", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_supply_charge") |> pull(amount)

y_approved_customer_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_approved", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_customer_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_approved_delivery_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_approved", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_delivery_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_approved_supply_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_approved", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_supply_charge") |> pull(amount)

y_doer_customer_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_doer", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_customer_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_doer_delivery_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_doer", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_delivery_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_doer_supply_charge <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_doer", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_elec_supply_charge") |> pull(amount)
y_doer_natural_gas <- annual_bills_by_component_plot |> filter(version == "hpr_doer", hvac == "mid_hp", charge_type == "annual_gas_bill") |> pull(amount)


# Savings and percentage savings
fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_approved <- y_approved_delivery_charge - y_baseline_delivery_charge
fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_approved_pct <- fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_approved / y_baseline_delivery_charge

fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_doer <- y_doer_delivery_charge - y_baseline_delivery_charge
fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_doer_pct <- fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_doer / y_baseline_delivery_charge

y_baseline_bill <- y_baseline_customer_charge + y_baseline_delivery_charge + y_baseline_supply_charge

fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_approved_pct_of_total_bill <- (fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_approved / y_baseline_bill * -100) |> round(0)

fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_doer_pct_of_total_bill <- (fig_stacked_bar_components_delivery_on_top_savings_doer / y_baseline_bill * -100) |> round(0)


y_annotation_offset <- 0
x_label_offset <- 3.5


fig_bill_stacked_bar_delivery_on_top <- ggplot(annual_bills_by_component_plot |>
  mutate(charge_type = factor(charge_type, levels = components)),
       aes(x = interaction(hvac, version), y = amount, fill = charge_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Components of Annual Electricity Bill",
       x = "",
       y = "Annual Cost ($)",
       fill = "Charge Type") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bill_component_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format(), limits = c(0, 4500), breaks = seq(0, 5000, by = 1000), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Current HVAC\nCurrent Rates",
                           "Mid-Efficiency HP\nCurrent Rates",
                           "Mid-Efficiency HP\n1.0 Rates",
                           "Mid-Efficiency HP\n2.0 Rates")) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "IBM-Plex-Sans"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 3)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 3)),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(t = 3, r = 200, b = 0, l = 10, unit = "pt")
  ) +

  # instead of a legend, write annotation for the 3 categories to the right of the right-most bar
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = x_label_offset,
    y = (y_doer_supply_charge/2) + y_annotation_offset,
    label = "Supply Charge",
    hjust = 0,
    family = "IBM-Plex-Sans",
    color = bill_component_colors["annual_elec_supply_charge"],
    size = 6,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = x_label_offset,
    y = (y_doer_customer_charge/1.6) + y_doer_supply_charge + y_annotation_offset,
    label = "Customer Charge",
    hjust = 0,
    family = "IBM-Plex-Sans",
    color = bill_component_colors["annual_elec_customer_charge"],
    size = 6,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = x_label_offset,
    y = (y_doer_delivery_charge/2) + y_doer_customer_charge + y_doer_supply_charge + y_annotation_offset,
    label = "Delivery Charge",
    hjust = 0,
    family = "IBM-Plex-Sans",
    color = bill_component_colors["annual_elec_delivery_charge"],
    size = 6,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  # No legend
  theme(legend.position = "none")

fig_bill_stacked_bar_delivery_on_top
```

## data-all-fuel-types
```{r}
#| label: data-all-fuel-types
########################################################
# Data
########################################################

# Parameters
bill_type <- 'annual_bill_change_energy'
electric_utility_option <- 'statewide'
baseline_heating_type_option <- 'All Fuels'

annual_change_all_fuel_types <- annual_change |>
  filter(electric_utility != "municipal") |>
  filter(!is.na(annual_bill_change) & is.finite(annual_bill_change),
        bill_type == !!bill_type,
        if (electric_utility_option != "statewide") electric_utility == !!electric_utility_option else TRUE,
        if (baseline_heating_type_option != "All Fuels") baseline_heating_type == !!baseline_heating_type_option else TRUE,
        year == !!supply_year
        )

# Print these to console
scenario_stats_all_fuel_types_low_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_all_fuel_types |> filter(electric_utility != "municipal"), hp_eff_for_stats = "low_hp", print_table = FALSE)
scenario_stats_all_fuel_types_mid_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_all_fuel_types |> filter(electric_utility != "municipal"), hp_eff_for_stats = "mid_hp", print_table = FALSE)
scenario_stats_all_fuel_types_high_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_all_fuel_types |> filter(electric_utility != "municipal"), hp_eff_for_stats = "high_hp", print_table = FALSE)
#
# These are the values used in the report!!!
# Calculate statistics for each version and set to the values used in the report
hp_eff_for_report <- "mid_hp"
scenario_stats_all_fuel_types <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_all_fuel_types |> filter(electric_utility != "municipal"),
                                                          hp_eff_for_stats = hp_eff_for_report,
                                                          print_table = FALSE)

# Save as variables to be exported then used in the report
versions <- list(
  list(version = "baseline", prefix = "default"),
  list(version = "hpr_approved", prefix = "approved"),
  list(version = "hpr_doer", prefix = "doer")
)

# Loop through versions to calculate statistics
for (v in versions) {
  # Get the stats for this version
  stats <- scenario_stats_all_fuel_types |>
    filter(version_elec == v$version)

  # Calculate and assign all statistics for this version
  # eg "baseline_median_bill_change", "approved_pct_that_save"...
  assign(paste0("median_bill_change_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_change), round_dollars))
  assign(paste0("pct_that_save_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(pct_that_save), round_percent))
  assign(paste0("pct_that_save_big_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(pct_that_save_big), round_percent))
  assign(paste0("pct_that_lose_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(pct_that_lose), round_percent))
  assign(paste0("pct_that_lose_big_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(pct_that_lose_big), round_percent))
  assign(paste0("median_savings_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_savings), round_dollars))
  assign(paste0("median_loss_", v$prefix, "_all_fuels"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_loss), round_dollars))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hists-all-fuel-types

Assumes default gas delivery rates, 2024 supply rates for gas and electricity, and 100% participation in low-income discount programs by eligible households."

########################################################
# Plots
########################################################
result_all_fuels <- plot_bill_change_histograms(
  annual_change_table = annual_change_all_fuel_types,
  bill_type = bill_type,
  baseline_heating_type_option = baseline_heating_type_option,
  electric_utility_option = electric_utility_option,
  supply_year = supply_year,
  second_subtitle = NULL,
  x_limits = c(-2500, 2500),
  y_limits = c(0, 200000)/242.13,
  binwidth = 100
)

# First return item is the plot
plot_all_fuels <- result_all_fuels[[1]]


# results[2-4] are the category percentages for baseline, approved, and doer, respectively.
# Here we assigned them to workspace variables for easy access in the report.
rate_versions <- list(
  list(name = "baseline", result_index = 2, prefix = "baseline"),
  list(name = "approved", result_index = 3, prefix = "approved"),
  list(name = "doer", result_index = 4, prefix = "doer")
)

# Loop through each rate version
for (version in rate_versions) {
  # Get the result for this version
  result <- result_all_fuels[[version$result_index]]

  # Extract large savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_all_fuel_type_", version$prefix, "_pct_large_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "large_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Extract small savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_all_fuel_type_", version$prefix, "_pct_small_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "small_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Calculate total savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_all_fuel_type_", version$prefix, "_pct_that_save"),
         result |>
           filter(bill_category == "small_savings" | bill_category == "large_savings") |>
           pull(percentage) |>
           sum() |>
           round(round_percent))
}

print(plot_all_fuels)
```

## ---------- How do savings vary by fuel? ----------
### fig-bar-fuel-types
```{r}
#| label: fig-bar-fuel-types
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of MA homes by primary heating fuel."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2

baseline_heating_type_counts_rs_raw <- get_housing_units_column_counts("electric_utility", "statewide")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# housing_units (ResStock)
baseline_heating_type_counts_rs_raw <- get_housing_units_column_counts("baseline_heating_type", "statewide")


baseline_heating_type_counts_rs <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs_raw |>
  mutate(rs_heating_type_group = case_when(
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Natural Gas") ~ "Natural Gas",
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Fuel Oil") ~ "Fuel Oil",
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Propane") ~ "Propane",
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Resistance") ~ "Resistance",
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Heat Pump") ~ "Heat Pump",
    baseline_heating_type %in% c("Other Fuel", "None") ~ "Other/None",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) |>
  mutate(rs_heating_type_group = factor(rs_heating_type_group,
                                   levels = c("Natural Gas", "Propane", "Fuel Oil",  "Heat Pump", "Resistance", "Other/None"))) |>
  group_by(rs_heating_type_group, .drop = FALSE) |>
  summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = count / sum(count),
         cum_pct = cumsum(pct),
         pct_label = paste0(rs_heating_type_group, ": ", scales::percent(pct, accuracy=1))
         )

pct_homes_natural_gas <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs |> filter(rs_heating_type_group == "Natural Gas") |> pull(pct)
pct_homes_fuel_oil <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs |> filter(rs_heating_type_group == "Fuel Oil") |> pull(pct)
pct_homes_propane <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs |> filter(rs_heating_type_group == "Propane") |> pull(pct)
pct_homes_electric_resistance <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs |> filter(rs_heating_type_group == "Resistance") |> pull(pct)

baseline_heating_type_counts_for_plot <- baseline_heating_type_counts_rs |>
  arrange((cum_pct)) |>
  mutate(
    # Start position is the cumulative percentage of previous segments
    start_pos = lag(cum_pct, default = 0),
    # End position is the cumulative percentage including current segment
    end_pos = cum_pct,
    # Center position for text labels
    label_pos = start_pos + pct/2
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = baseline_heating_type_counts_for_plot,
    aes(xmin = start_pos, xmax = end_pos, ymin = 0.85, ymax = 1.15, fill = rs_heating_type_group)
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = baseline_heating_type_counts_for_plot,
    aes(x = label_pos, y = 1, label = pct_label, color = rs_heating_type_group),
    direction = "y",
    nudge_y = 0.15,
    nudge_x = 0.005,
    size = 3,
    segment.size = 0.0,
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = 0,
    angle = 30
  ) +
  xlim(0, 1.2) +
  ylim(0.8, 1.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = heating_type_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = heating_type_colors) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
annual_change_heating_oil <- annual_change |>
  filter(electric_utility != "municipal") |>
  filter(!is.na(annual_bill_change) & is.finite(annual_bill_change),
        bill_type == !!bill_type,
        if (electric_utility_option != "statewide") electric_utility == !!electric_utility_option else TRUE,
        if (baseline_heating_type_option != "all") baseline_heating_type == !!baseline_heating_type_option else TRUE,
        year == supply_year)

# Print these to console
scenario_stats_natural_gas_low_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_heating_oil, "low_hp", print_table = FALSE)
scenario_stats_natural_gas_mid_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_heating_oil, "mid_hp", print_table = FALSE)
scenario_stats_natural_gas_high_hp <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_heating_oil, "high_hp", print_table = FALSE)
#
#
#
# These are the values used in the report!!!
# Calculate statistics for each version and set to the values used in the report
hp_eff_for_report <- "mid_hp"
scenario_stats_heating_oil <- calc_stats_by_rate_version(annual_change_heating_oil, hp_eff_for_report, print_table = FALSE)

versions <- list(
  list(version = "baseline", prefix = "default"),
  list(version = "hpr_approved", prefix = "approved"),
  list(version = "hpr_doer", prefix = "doer")
)

# Loop through versions to calculate statistics
for (v in versions) {
  # Get the stats for this version
  stats <- scenario_stats_heating_oil |>
    filter(version_elec == v$version)

  # Calculate and assign all statistics for this version
  assign(paste0("median_bill_change_", v$prefix, "_heating_oil"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_change), round_dollars))
  assign(paste0("pct_that_save_", v$prefix, "_heating_oil"),
         round(stats |> pull(pct_that_save), round_percent))
  assign(paste0("median_savings_", v$prefix, "_heating_oil"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_savings), round_dollars))
  assign(paste0("median_loss_", v$prefix, "_heating_oil"),
         round(stats |> pull(median_loss), round_dollars))
}


########################################################
# Plots
########################################################
result_heating_oil <- plot_bill_change_histograms(
  annual_change_table = annual_change_heating_oil,
  bill_type = bill_type,
  baseline_heating_type_option = baseline_heating_type_option,
  electric_utility_option = electric_utility_option,
  supply_year = supply_year,
  #second_subtitle = "Fuel Oil Heating",
  x_limits = c(-2500, 2500),
  y_limits = c(0, 50000)/242.13,
  binwidth = 100
)

# First return item is the plot
plot_heating_oil <- result_heating_oil[[1]]


# results[2-4] are the category percentages for baseline, approved, and doer, respectively.
# Here we assigned them to workspace variables for easy access in the report.
rate_versions <- list(
  list(name = "baseline", result_index = 2, prefix = "baseline"),
  list(name = "approved", result_index = 3, prefix = "approved"),
  list(name = "doer", result_index = 4, prefix = "doer")
)

# Loop through each rate version
for (version in rate_versions) {
  # Get the result for this version
  result <- result_heating_oil[[version$result_index]]

  # Extract large savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_heating_oil_", version$prefix, "_pct_large_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "large_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Extract small savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_heating_oil_", version$prefix, "_pct_small_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "small_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Calculate total savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_heating_oil_", version$prefix, "_pct_that_save"),
         result |>
           filter(bill_category == "small_savings" | bill_category == "large_savings") |>
           pull(percentage) |>
           sum() |>
           round(round_percent))
}

print(plot_heating_oil)
```

## ---------- How do savings vary by building type? ----------
### data-building-type
```{r}
#| label: data-building-type
annual_change_bldg_type <- annual_change |>
  mutate(
    building_type_group = case_when(
      building_type %in% c("Single-Family Detached", "Mobile Home", "Single-Family Attached") ~ "Single-Family",
      building_type %in% c("2 Unit", "3 or 4 Unit") ~ "2-4 Units",
      building_type %in% c("5 to 9 Unit", "10 to 19 Unit", "20 to 49 Unit", "50 or more Unit") ~ "5+ Units",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
  )

# Create box plots by building type and version_elec
building_type_group_order = c("Single-Family", "2-4 Units", "5+ Units")

building_type_group_names = c("Single-Family", "2-4 Units", "5+ Units")

data_box_building_type <- annual_change_bldg_type |>
  filter(!is.na(annual_bill_change) & is.finite(annual_bill_change),
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_energy",
        raw_or_discounted == "discounted",
        building_type_group %in% building_type_group_order)

# Convert building_type to factor with specified order
data_box_building_type <- data_box_building_type |>
  mutate(building_type_group = factor(building_type_group, levels = building_type_group_order))

# Calculate custom boxplot stats for each group
box_building_type_stats <- data_box_building_type |>
  group_by(building_type_group, version_elec) |>
  summarise(
    data_min   = min(annual_bill_change, na.rm = TRUE),                # lower whisker
    lower  = quantile(annual_bill_change, 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),     # lower hinge (Q1)
    middle = median(annual_bill_change, na.rm = TRUE),             # median
    upper  = quantile(annual_bill_change, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),     # upper hinge (Q3)
    data_max   = max(annual_bill_change, na.rm = TRUE),                # upper whisker
    pct_that_save = mean(annual_bill_change < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_savings = median(annual_bill_change[annual_bill_change < 0], na.rm = TRUE),  # median of negative values (savings)
    .groups = "drop",
  )

```

### fig-stacked-bar-building-type
```{r}
#| label: fig-stacked-bar-building-type
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of MA homes by building type."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 1

# Get counts of buildings by type
building_counts <- data_box_building_type |>
  group_by(building_type_group) |>
  summarise(n = n_distinct(bldg_id)) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  arrange(match(building_type_group, building_type_group_order))

# Calculate placement for labels
building_counts <- building_counts |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n),
    pct_label = paste0(building_type_group, ": ", scales::percent(pct, accuracy=1)),
    cum_pct = cumsum(pct),
    placement = cum_pct
  )

building_counts_for_plot <- building_counts |>
  mutate(
    # Start position is the cumulative percentage of previous segments
    start_pos = lag(cum_pct, default = 0),
    # End position is the cumulative percentage including current segment
    end_pos = cum_pct,
    # Center position for text labels
    center_pos = (start_pos + end_pos) / 2
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = building_counts_for_plot,
    aes(xmin = start_pos, xmax = end_pos, ymin = 0.85, ymax = 1.15, fill = building_type_group)
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = building_counts_for_plot,
    aes(x = end_pos-0.005, y = 1, label = pct_label, color = building_type_group),
    direction = "y",
    nudge_y = 0.2,
    nudge_x = -0.05,
    size = 3,
    segment.size = 0.0,
    hjust = .8,
    vjust = 0.5
  ) +
  xlim(0, 1.2) +
  ylim(0.8, 1.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = housing_type_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = housing_type_colors) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}
  list(name = "approved", result_index = 3, prefix = "approved"),
  list(name = "doer", result_index = 4, prefix = "doer")
)

# Loop through each rate version
for (version in rate_versions) {
  # Get the result for this version
  result <- result_5_plus_units[[version$result_index]]

  # Extract large savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_5_plus_units_", version$prefix, "_pct_large_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "large_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Extract small savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_5_plus_units_", version$prefix, "_pct_small_savings"),
         round(result |> filter(bill_category == "small_savings") |> pull(percentage), round_percent))

  # Calculate total savings percentage
  assign(paste0("fig_hists_5_plus_units_", version$prefix, "_pct_that_save"),
         result |>
           filter(bill_category == "small_savings" | bill_category == "large_savings") |>
           pull(percentage) |>
           sum() |>
           round(round_percent))
}

print(plot_5_plus_units)
```

### fig-hists-impact-of-low-income-discounts
```{r}
#| label: fig-hists-impact-of-low-income-discounts
#|

plot_li_discount_histograms <- function(
  datasets,
  hvac_for_utility_bills,
  incomes_threshold,
  x_limits = c(0, 0.2),
  y_limits = c(0, 150000/242.13),
  binwidth = 0.01
) {
  # # Define dataset list with names for easy processing
  # datasets <- list(
  #   "Baseline Rates, Current HVAC, 100% Participation" = li_baseline_rates_current_hvac_100pct_participation,
  #   "Baseline Rates, Current HVAC, 0% Participation" = li_baseline_rates_current_hvac_0pct_participation,
  #   "Baseline Rates, Mid HP, Undiscounted" = li_baseline_undiscounted,
  #   "Baseline Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = li_baseline_discounted,
  #   "Approved Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = li_hpr_approved_discounted,
  #   "DOER Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = li_hpr_doer_discounted
  # )

  # Define color palette for each dataset
  colors <- c(
    "Baseline Rates, Current HVAC, 100% Participation" = "magenta",
    "Baseline Rates, Current HVAC, 0% Participation" = "red",
    "Baseline Rates, Mid HP, Undiscounted" = "grey50",
    "Baseline Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = "#023047",
    "Approved Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = "#FC9706",
    "DOER Rates, Mid HP, Discounted" = "#68BED8"
  )

  # Calculate y_max across all datasets if not provided
  if (is.null(y_limits)) {
    y_max <- 10
    for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
      hist_plot <- ggplot(datasets[[dataset_name]], aes(x = energy_burden)) +
        geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth)

      current_max <- max(ggplot_build(hist_plot)$data[[1]]$count, na.rm = TRUE)
      y_max <- max(y_max, current_max)
    }

    y_max <- ceiling(y_max * 1.1)
    y_limits <- c(0, y_max)
  }

  #Function to create a single histogram for a dataset
  create_single_histogram <- function(data, name, is_first = FALSE, is_last = FALSE) {
    low_burden_threshold <- 0.04
    moderate_burden_threshold <- 0.06
    high_burden_threshold <- 0.12


    # Calculate bill categories
    data <- data |>
      mutate(bill_category = case_when(
        energy_burden < low_burden_threshold ~ "low_energy_burden",
        energy_burden < moderate_burden_threshold ~ "moderate_energy_burden",
        energy_burden < high_burden_threshold ~ "high_energy_burden",
        TRUE ~ "very_high_energy_burden"
      ))

    # Calculate percentages for each category
    category_percentages <- data |>
      group_by(bill_category) |>
      summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(percentage = count / sum(count) * 100)

    # Get percentages for annotation
    pct_low_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "low_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_moderate_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "moderate_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_high_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "high_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_very_high_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "very_high_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    # Calculate bin breaks and midpoints
    breaks <- seq(floor(x_limits[1]/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(x_limits[2]/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)

    # Manually bin the data
    binned_data <- data |>
      mutate(bin = cut(energy_burden,
                      breaks = breaks,
                      include.lowest = TRUE,
                      right = FALSE)) |>
      group_by(bin, bill_category) |>
      summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
      # Add bin midpoint for plotting
      mutate(bin_mid = as.numeric(as.character(
        sapply(bin, function(b) {
          # Extract bin boundaries and calculate midpoint
          vals <- as.numeric(gsub("\\(|\\]|\\[|\\)", "", strsplit(as.character(b), ",")[[1]]))
          return(mean(vals))
        })
      )))

    # More balanced color palette
    dark_red <- "#db8b87"        # dark red
    light_red <- "#eaada9"       # light red
    light_green <- "#8ebd85"     # light green
    dark_green <- "#5e8a5e"      # dark green

    # Position the bars at the top and text just below
    bar_y_pos <- y_limits[2]
    text_y_pos <- y_limits[2] * 0.90

    # Calculate x positions for percentage labels
    x_low_energy_burden <- mean(c(0, low_burden_threshold-0.002))
    x_moderate_energy_burden <- mean(c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold))
    x_high_energy_burden <- mean(c(moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold))
    x_very_high_energy_burden <- mean(c(high_burden_threshold, x_limits[2]))

    # Create the plot
    plot <- ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = bin_mid, y = count, fill = bill_category)) +
      # Add vertical dotted lines at the category boundaries
      geom_vline(xintercept = c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", size = 0.5) +

      # Add the bars
      geom_col(position = "stack", width = binwidth * 0.9) +

      # Set the fill colors
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "low_energy_burden" = dark_green,
          "moderate_energy_burden" = light_green,
          "high_energy_burden" = light_red,
          "very_high_energy_burden" = dark_red
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +

      # Add horizontal colored lines at the top
      annotate("segment",
                x = x_limits[1], xend = low_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = dark_green, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = low_burden_threshold, xend = moderate_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = light_green, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = moderate_burden_threshold, xend = high_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = light_red, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = high_burden_threshold, xend = x_limits[2],
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = dark_red, size = 1) +

      # Add percentage labels
      annotate("text",
                x = x_low_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
                label = paste0(pct_low_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_moderate_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
                label = paste0(pct_moderate_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_high_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
                label = paste0(pct_high_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_very_high_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
                label = paste0(pct_very_high_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      # Add dataset name on the right
      annotate("text",
                x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
                y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
                label = name,
                hjust = 1,
                fontface = "bold",
                size = 3,
                color = colors[name]) +

      # Format axes
      scale_y_continuous(
        labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 242.13 * 0.001), "k"),
        name = "# of Homes",
        limits = y_limits,
        breaks = c(0, 50000, 100000, 150000)/242.13
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
        name = "Energy Burden",
        limits = x_limits,
        breaks = c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold)
      ) +

      # Apply theme
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = 0.15
      )

    # Configure axes based on position
    if (!is_last) {
      plot <- plot +
        theme(
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
        )
    }
    return(list(plot, category_percentages))
  }


  # Create each histogram
  dataset_names <- names(datasets)
  plots <- list()
  list_of_category_percentages <- list()
  for (i in 1:length(datasets)) {
    name <- dataset_names[i]
    is_first <- (i == 1)
    is_last <- (i == length(datasets))

    result_single_histogram <- create_single_histogram(
      data = datasets[[name]],
      name = name,
      is_first = is_first,
      is_last = is_last
    )

    plots[[i]] <- result_single_histogram[[1]]
    list_of_category_percentages[[i]] <- result_single_histogram[[2]]
  }

  # Combine plots with patchwork
  combined_plot <- plots[[1]]
  for (i in 2:length(plots)) {
    combined_plot <- combined_plot / plots[[i]]
  }

  # Add overall title and formatting
  final_plot <- combined_plot +
    plot_layout(
      heights = rep(1, length(plots)),
      guides = "collect"
    ) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Winter Energy Burdens in Massachusetts, by Scenario",
      subtitle = paste0("Among households below $", incomes_threshold),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
        plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5, "pt")
      )
    ) &
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      plot.margin = margin(1, 5, 1, 5, "pt")
    )

  return(list(final_plot, list_of_category_percentages))
}

# ---------
# Function Inputs

datasets <- list(
  "Current HVAC, 100% Discounts, Default Rates" = li_baseline_rates_current_hvac_100pct_participation,
  "Current HVAC, 0% Discounts, Default Rates" = li_baseline_rates_current_hvac_0pct_participation,
  "ccASHP, 0% Discounts, Default Rates" = li_baseline_undiscounted,
  "ccASHP, 100% Discounts, Default Rates" = li_baseline_discounted,
  "ccASHP, 100% Discounts, 1.0 Rates" = li_hpr_approved_discounted,
  "ccASHP, 100% Discounts, 2.0 Rates" = li_hpr_doer_discounted
)





# ---------
# Actually use the function
result_li_discount_histograms <- plot_li_discount_histograms(
  datasets,
  incomes_threshold = incomes_threshold,
  x_limits = c(0, 0.2),
  y_limits = c(0, 150000/242.13),
  binwidth = 0.01
)

# Extract results with different variable names
combined_plot <- result_li_discount_histograms[[1]]
list_of_category_percentages <- result_li_discount_histograms[[2]]

# Display the plot
print(combined_plot)

# Fix the rate_versions to match your actual datasets
rate_versions <- list(
  list(name = "baseline_undiscounted", result_index = 3, prefix = "baseline_undiscounted"),
  list(name = "baseline_discounted", result_index = 4, prefix = "baseline_discounted"),
  list(name = "approved", result_index = 5, prefix = "approved"),
  list(name = "doer", result_index = 6, prefix = "doer")
)

# Fix the category name and loop structure
for (i in seq_along(datasets)) {
  dataset_name <- names(datasets)[i]
  dataset_name <- tolower(gsub("[,]", "", dataset_name))
  dataset_name <- tolower(gsub("[%]", "pct", dataset_name))
  dataset_name <- tolower(gsub("__", "_", dataset_name))
  # Get the result for this dataset
  result <- list_of_category_percentages[[i]]

  # Use the correct category names from your function
  for (category in c("low_energy_burden", "moderate_energy_burden", "high_energy_burden", "very_high_energy_burden")) {
    pct_value <- result |>
      filter(bill_category == category) |>
      pull(percentage)

    if (length(pct_value) > 0) {
      assign(paste0("fig_hists_li_discount_histograms_", gsub(" ", "_", dataset_name), "_", category),
             round(pct_value, round_percent))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
  # Calculate bin breaks and midpoints
  breaks <- seq(floor(x_limits[1]/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(x_limits[2]/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)

  # Manually bin the data
  binned_data <- data |>
    mutate(bin = cut(energy_burden,
                    breaks = breaks,
                    include.lowest = TRUE,
                    right = FALSE)) |>
    group_by(bin, bill_category) |>

    mutate(bin_mid = as.numeric(as.character(

      })
    )))

  # More balanced color palette
  dark_red <- "#db8b87"
  light_red <- "#eaada9"
  light_green <- "#8ebd85"
  dark_green <- "#5e8a5e"

  # Position the bars at the top and text just below
  bar_y_pos <- y_limits[2]
  text_y_pos <- y_limits[2] * 0.90

  # Calculate x positions for percentage labels
  x_low_energy_burden <- mean(c(0, low_burden_threshold-0.002))
  x_moderate_energy_burden <- mean(c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold))
  x_high_energy_burden <- mean(c(moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold))

        "moderate_energy_burden" = light_green,
        "high_energy_burden" = light_red,
        "very_high_energy_burden" = dark_red
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    # Add vertical lines at the category boundaries
    annotate("segment",
              x = x_limits[1], xend = low_burden_threshold,
              y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
              color = dark_green, size = 1) +
    annotate("segment",
              x = low_burden_threshold, xend = moderate_burden_threshold,
              y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
              color = light_green, size = 1) +
    annotate("segment",
              x = moderate_burden_threshold, xend = high_burden_threshold,
              y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
              color = light_red, size = 1) +
    annotate("segment",
              x = high_burden_threshold, xend = x_limits[2],
              y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
              color = dark_red, size = 1) +
    annotate("text",
              x = x_low_energy_burden,
              y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
              label = paste0(pct_low_energy_burden, "%"),
              size = 3,
              fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text",
              x = x_moderate_energy_burden,
              y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
              label = paste0(pct_moderate_energy_burden, "%"),
              size = 3,
              fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text",
              x = x_high_energy_burden,
              y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
              label = paste0(pct_high_energy_burden, "%"),
              size = 3,
              fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text",
              x = x_very_high_energy_burden,
              y = text_y_pos * 0.95,
              label = paste0(pct_very_high_energy_burden, "%"),
              size = 3,
              fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text",
              x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
              y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
              label = name,
              hjust = 1,
              fontface = "bold",
              size = 3,
              color = colors[name]) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 242.13 * 0.001), "k"),
      #name = "# of Homes",
      limits = y_limits,
      breaks = c(0, 50000, 100000, 150000)/242.13
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      name = "Winter Energy Burden",
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold),
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      aspect.ratio = 0.18,  # CHANGED: Increased from 0.15 to match bill change histograms
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8)
    )

  # Remove x-axis elements if requested
  if (!show_x_axis) {
    plot <- plot +
      theme(
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )
  }

  # Remove y-axis elements if requested
  if (!show_y_axis) {
    plot <- plot +
      theme(
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
      )
  }

  return(plot)
}

```

## ---------- How do savings vary by utility? ----------
### fig-stacked-bars-utility-rate-scenarios (fig16)
```{r}
#| label: fig-stacked-bars-utility-rate-scenarios
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of MA homes served by each investor-owned electric utility that would see a large or small bill savings or increase in total winter energy bills when switching to heat pumps, under default vs. 1.0 vs. 2.0 heat pump electric delivery rates. Assumes default gas delivery rates, 2024 supply rates for gas and electricity, and 100% participation in low-income programs by eligible households."

# Create a function to categorize bill changes
categorize_bill_changes_by_utility <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    filter(bill_type == "annual_bill_change_energy",
           hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills,
           version_elec %in% c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")) %>%
    mutate(category = case_when(
      annual_bill_change <= -1000 ~ "large_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 0 ~ "small_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 1000 ~ "small_increase",
      TRUE ~ "large_increase"
    )) %>%
    group_by(electric_utility, version_elec, category) %>%
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(electric_utility, version_elec) %>%
    mutate(
      total = sum(count),
      percentage = count / total * 100,
      utility_scenario = paste(electric_utility, version_elec, sep = "_")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Apply the function to the data
utility_scenario_counts <- categorize_bill_changes_by_utility(annual_change_with_municipal)

# Set factor levels for correct ordering
utility_scenario_counts <- utility_scenario_counts %>%
  mutate(
    # FIXED: Order for stacking - this controls the visual stacking order
    # For negative values, the order is visually reversed, so we put large_savings before small_savings
    category = factor(
      category,
      levels = c("large_increase", "small_increase", "large_savings", "small_savings")
    ),
    electric_utility = factor(
      electric_utility,
      levels = c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil", "municipal")
    ),
    version_elec = factor(
      version_elec,
      levels = c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")
    ),
    utility_scenario = factor(
      utility_scenario,
      levels = paste(rep(c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil", "municipal"), each = 3),
                    rep(c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer"), 4),
                    sep = "_")
    )
  )

# Create the stacked bar chart
ggplot(utility_scenario_counts, aes(x = utility_scenario, y = percentage, fill = category)) +
  # Reference line at 0 (boundary between savings and increases)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # For savings categories (plotted downward)
  geom_col(
    data = utility_scenario_counts %>% filter(category %in% c("large_savings", "small_savings")),
    aes(y = -percentage),
    position = "stack"
  ) +
  # For increase categories (plotted upward)
  geom_col(
    data = utility_scenario_counts %>% filter(category %in% c("small_increase", "large_increase")),
    position = "stack"
  ) +
  # Add percentage labels for savings (negative values)
  geom_text(
    data = utility_scenario_counts %>% filter(category %in% c("large_savings", "small_savings")),
    aes(y = -percentage, label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  # Add percentage labels for increases (positive values)
  geom_text(
    data = utility_scenario_counts %>% filter(category %in% c("small_increase", "large_increase")),
    aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  # FIXED: Swapped the colors for increase categories
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "large_savings" = "#5e8a5e",      # dark green
      "small_savings" = "#8ebd85",      # light green
      "small_increase" = "#eaada9",     # FIXED: now light red (was dark red)
      "large_increase" = "#db8b87"      # FIXED: now dark red (was light red)
    ),
    labels = c(
      "large_savings" = ">$1,000 savings",
      "small_savings" = "$0-$1,000 savings",
      "small_increase" = "$0-$1,000 increase",
      "large_increase" = ">$1,000 increase"
    ),
    breaks = c("large_increase", "small_increase", "small_savings", "large_savings")
  ) +
  # Add utility grouping
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = NULL,
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = rep(c("Default", "1.0", "2.0 rates"), 4),
    guide = guide_axis(n.dodge = 1)
  ) +
  # Add utility labels with faceting
  facet_wrap(
    ~ factor(electric_utility,
            levels = c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil", "municipal"),
            labels = c("Eversource", "National Grid", "Unitil", "Municipal")),
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in Total Winter Energy Bills when Switching to Heat Pump, by Utility",
    subtitle = glue::glue("{supply_year} Supply Prices"),
    x = NULL,
    y = "",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# Create and export report variables for each utility, scenario, and category combination
for (utility in c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil", "municipal")) {
  for (scenario in c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")) {
    for (category in c("large_savings", "small_savings", "large_increase", "small_increase")) {
      # Get the percentage for this specific combination
      pct_value <- utility_scenario_counts |>
        filter(electric_utility == utility & version_elec == scenario & category == !!category) |>
        pull(percentage)

      # Handle cases where the category might not exist (assign 0)
      if (length(pct_value) == 0) {
        pct_value <- 0
      }

      # Create variable name like: utility_scenario_counts_eversource_baseline_large_savings
      var_name <- paste("utility_change_", utility, "_", scenario, "_", category, sep = "")
      assign(var_name, round(pct_value, round_percent))
    }
  }
}

```

### fig-boxplot-utility-bills (fig17)
```{r}
#| label: fig-boxplot-utility-bills
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of total winter energy bills, for all MA homes served by an investor-owned electric utility, before and after switching to heat pumps, under default vs. 1.0 vs. 2.0 heat pump electric delivery rates, by utility. Assumes default gas delivery rates, 2024 supply rates for gas and electricity, and 100% participation in low-income programs by eligible households."

# Prepare the data for boxplots (exclude municipal)
utility_bills_boxplot <- annual_bills_with_municipal |>
  filter(
    bill_type == "annual_bill_energy",
    raw_or_discounted == "discounted",
    electric_utility %in% c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil")  # Remove municipal
  ) |>
  mutate(scenario = case_when(
      hvac == 'current' & version_elec == "baseline" ~ "baseline_rates_current_hvac",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "baseline" ~ "baseline",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "hpr_approved" ~ "hpr_approved",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "hpr_doer" ~ "hpr_doer",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(scenario)) |>
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(
      scenario,
      levels = c(
        "hpr_doer",
        "hpr_approved",
        "baseline",
        "baseline_rates_current_hvac"
      )
    ),
    electric_utility = factor(electric_utility,
                            levels = c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil"))
  )

# Loop through versions to calculate statistics
for (eu in c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil")) {
  for (s in c("baseline_rates_current_hvac", "baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")) {
    # Get the stats for this version
    stats <- utility_bills_boxplot |>
      filter(electric_utility == eu) |>
      filter(scenario == s) |>
      summarise(
        p25 = quantile(annual_bill, 0.25),
        p50 = quantile(annual_bill, 0.50),
        p75 = quantile(annual_bill, 0.75)
      )
    assign(paste0("utility_bills_", eu, "_", s, "_p25"),
           round(stats |> pull(p25), round_dollars))
    assign(paste0("utility_bills_", eu, "_", s, "_p50"),
           round(stats |> pull(p50), round_dollars))
    assign(paste0("utility_bills_", eu, "_", s, "_p75"),
           round(stats |> pull(p75), round_dollars))
  }
}

# Create the boxplot with flipped axes and no outliers
ggplot(utility_bills_boxplot, aes(y = electric_utility, x = annual_bill, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
    alpha = 0.8,
    outlier.shape = NA  # Remove outliers but keep whiskers
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "baseline_rates_current_hvac" = "grey50",
      "baseline" = "#023047",
      "hpr_approved" = "#FC9706",
      "hpr_doer" = "#68BED8"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "baseline_rates_current_hvac" = "Baseline Rates, Current HVAC",
      "baseline" = "Baseline Rates, Mid HP",
      "hpr_approved" = "Heat Pump, 1.0 HP Rates",
      "hpr_doer" = "Heat Pump, 2.0 HP Rates"
    )
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "eversource" = "Eversource",
      "nationalgrid" = "National Grid",
      "unitil" = "Unitil"
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.3, 0.3))  # Add space at top for labels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0.05)),
    limits = c(0, 8000)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Winter Energy Bills by Utility and Scenario",
    subtitle = "Vertical lines represent 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles; outliers removed",
    y = NULL,
    x = "Annual Energy Bill",
    fill = "Scenario"
  ) +
    # Add colored annotations instead of legend
  annotate("text", x = 5600, y = 3.39, label = "Current HVAC, Default Rates",
           color = "grey50", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 5500, y = 3.19, label = "Heat Pump, Default Rates",
           color = "#023047", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 5400, y = 2.99, label = "Heat Pump, 1.0 HP Rates",
           color = "#FC9706", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 5300, y = 2.78, label = "Heat Pump, 2.0 HP Rates",
           color = "#68BED8", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, color = "gray60"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    aspect.ratio = 0.5,
    plot.margin = margin(t = 0.05, r = 0.1, b = 0.05, l = 0.1),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"  # Remove the legend
  )

```

```{r}
    electric_utility %in% c("municipal", "eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil")
  ) |>
  mutate(scenario = case_when(
      hvac == 'current' & version_elec == "baseline" ~ "baseline_rates_current_hvac",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "baseline" ~ "baseline",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "hpr_approved" ~ "hpr_approved",
      hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills & version_elec == "hpr_doer" ~ "hpr_doer",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(scenario)) |>
  filter(!(scenario %in% c("baseline_rates_current_hvac", "hpr_approved"))) |>
  mutate(
    annual_bill = ifelse(electric_utility == "municipal" & scenario == "hpr_doer", 0, annual_bill),
    scenario = factor(
      scenario,
      levels = c(
        "hpr_doer",
        "baseline"
      )
    ),
    electric_utility = factor(electric_utility,
                            levels = c("municipal", "eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil"))
  )

# Create the boxplot with flipped axes and no outliers
ggplot(utility_bills_boxplot, aes(y = electric_utility, x = annual_bill, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
    alpha = 0.8,
    outlier.shape = NA  # Remove outliers but keep whiskers
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "baseline" = "#023047",
      "hpr_doer" = "#68BED8"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "baseline" = "Heat Pump, Default Rates",
      "hpr_doer" = "Heat Pump, 2.0 HP Rates"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "municipal" = "Municipal Light Plants",
      "eversource" = "Eversource",
      "nationalgrid" = "National Grid",
      "unitil" = "Unitil"
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.3))  # Add space at top for labels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0.05)),
    limits = c(0, 8000)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Winter Energy Bills, by Utility ",
    subtitle = "Vertical lines represent 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles; outliers removed",
    y = NULL,
    x = "Annual Energy Bill",
    fill = "Scenario"
  ) +
  # Add colored annotations instead of legend
  annotate("text", x = 5300, y = 4.06, label = "Heat Pump, Default Rates",
           color = "#023047", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 4200, y = 3.66, label = "Heat Pump, 2.0 HP Rates",
           color = "#68BED8", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, color = "gray60"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    aspect.ratio = 0.5,
    plot.margin = margin(t = 0.05, r = 0.1, b = 0.05, l = 0.1),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"  # Remove the legend
  )
```

### fig-hists-edc-mlp-burden
```{r}
#| label: fig-hists-edc-mlp-burden
#| fig-cap: "fig-hists-edc-mlp-burden"

plot_edc_mlp_burden_histograms <- function(
  datasets,
  hvac_for_utility_bills,
  x_limits = c(0, 0.2),
  y_limits = NULL,
  binwidth = 0.01
) {
  # Define color palette for each dataset
  colors <- c(
    "EDC Baseline" = "grey50",
    "EDC Approved" = "#d13b40",
    "EDC DOER" = "#023047",
    "MLP Baseline" = "#FC9706"
  )

  # # Calculate y_max across all datasets if not provided
  # if (is.null(y_limits)) {
  #   y_max <- 10
  #   for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  #     hist_plot <- ggplot(datasets[[dataset_name]], aes(x = energy_burden)) +
  #       geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth)

  #     current_max <- max(ggplot_build(hist_plot)$data[[1]]$count, na.rm = TRUE)
  #     y_max <- max(y_max, current_max)
  #   }

  #   y_max <- ceiling(y_max * 1.1)
  #
  # }



  # Function to create a single histogram for a dataset
  create_single_histogram <- function(data, name, is_first = FALSE, is_last = FALSE) {
    low_burden_threshold <- 0.04
    moderate_burden_threshold <- 0.06
    high_burden_threshold <- 0.12

    # Calculate bill categories based on energy burden
    data <- data |>
      mutate(bill_category = case_when(
        energy_burden < low_burden_threshold ~ "low_energy_burden",
        energy_burden < moderate_burden_threshold ~ "moderate_energy_burden",
        energy_burden < high_burden_threshold ~ "high_energy_burden",
        TRUE ~ "very_high_energy_burden"
      ))

    # Calculate percentages for each category
    category_percentages <- data |>
      group_by(bill_category) |>
      summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(percentage = count / sum(count) * 100)

    # Get percentages for annotation
    pct_low_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "low_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_moderate_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "moderate_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_high_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "high_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    pct_very_high_energy_burden <- category_percentages |>
      filter(bill_category == "very_high_energy_burden") |>
      pull(percentage) |>
      round(1)

    # Calculate bin breaks and midpoints
    breaks <- seq(floor(x_limits[1]/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(x_limits[2]/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)

    # Manually bin the data
    binned_data <- data |>
      mutate(bin = cut(energy_burden,
                      breaks = breaks,
                      include.lowest = TRUE,
                      right = FALSE)) |>
      group_by(bin, bill_category) |>
      summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
      # Add bin midpoint for plotting
      mutate(bin_mid = as.numeric(as.character(
        sapply(bin, function(b) {
          # Extract bin boundaries and calculate midpoint
          vals <- as.numeric(gsub("\\(|\\]|\\[|\\)", "", strsplit(as.character(b), ",")[[1]]))
          return(mean(vals))
        })
      )))

    # Color palette for energy burden categories
    dark_red <- "#db8b87"        # dark red
    light_red <- "#eaada9"       # light red
    light_green <- "#8ebd85"     # light green
    dark_green <- "#5e8a5e"      # dark green

    # Position the bars at the top and text just below
    bar_y_pos <- y_limits[2]
    text_y_pos <- y_limits[2] * 0.90

    # Calculate x positions for percentage labels
    x_low_energy_burden <- mean(c(0, low_burden_threshold-0.002))
    x_moderate_energy_burden <- mean(c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold))
    x_high_energy_burden <- mean(c(moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold))
    x_very_high_energy_burden <- mean(c(high_burden_threshold, x_limits[2]))


    # # Calculate y_max dynamically based on highest bin count
    # y_max <- binned_data |>
    #   group_by(bin_mid) |>
    #   summarise(total_count = sum(count)) |>
    #   pull(total_count) |>
    #   max() |>
    #   {function(x) ceiling(x/(25000/242.13))*(25000/242.13)}()

    # # Update y_limits with new y_max
    # y_limits <- c(0, y_max)

    # Set y_max based on plot number
    if (name == "MLP Baseline") {
      y_max <- 120000/242.13
      y_tick_step <- 50000
    } else {
      y_max <- 850000/242.13
      y_tick_step <- 250000
    }

    y_limits <- c(0, y_max)

    # Recalculate bar and text positions with new y_max
    bar_y_pos <- y_max
    text_y_pos <- y_max * 0.90

    # Create the plot
    plot <- ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = bin_mid, y = count, fill = bill_category)) +
      # Add vertical dotted lines at the category boundaries
      geom_vline(xintercept = c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", size = 0.5) +

      # Add the bars
      geom_col(position = "stack", width = binwidth * 0.9) +

      # Set the fill colors
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "low_energy_burden" = dark_green,
          "moderate_energy_burden" = light_green,
          "high_energy_burden" = light_red,
          "very_high_energy_burden" = dark_red
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +

      # Add horizontal colored lines at the top
      annotate("segment",
                x = x_limits[1], xend = low_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = dark_green, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = low_burden_threshold, xend = moderate_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = light_green, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = moderate_burden_threshold, xend = high_burden_threshold,
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = light_red, size = 1) +

      annotate("segment",
                x = high_burden_threshold, xend = x_limits[2],
                y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
                color = dark_red, size = 1) +

      # Add percentage labels
      annotate("text",
                x = x_low_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos,
                label = paste0(pct_low_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_moderate_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos,
                label = paste0(pct_moderate_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_high_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos,
                label = paste0(pct_high_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      annotate("text",
                x = x_very_high_energy_burden,
                y = text_y_pos,
                label = paste0(pct_very_high_energy_burden, "%"),
                size = 3,
                fontface = "bold") +

      # Add dataset name on the right
      annotate("text",
                x = x_limits[2] * 0.95,
                y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
                label = name,
                hjust = 1,
                fontface = "bold",
                size = 3,
                color = colors[name]) +

      # Format axes
      scale_y_continuous(
        labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 242.13 * 0.001), "k"),
        name = "# of Homes",
        limits = y_limits,
        breaks = seq(0, y_max*242.13, by = y_tick_step)/242.13
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
        name = "Energy Burden",
        limits = x_limits,
        breaks = c(low_burden_threshold, moderate_burden_threshold, high_burden_threshold)
      ) +

      # Apply theme
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = 0.15
      )

    # Configure axes based on position
    if (!is_last) {
      plot <- plot +
        theme(
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
        )
    }
    return(list(plot, category_percentages))
  }

  # Create each histogram
  dataset_names <- names(datasets)
  plots <- list()
  list_of_category_percentages <- list()

  for (i in 1:length(datasets)) {
    name <- dataset_names[i]
    is_first <- (i == 1)
    is_last <- (i == length(datasets))

    result_single_histogram <- create_single_histogram(
      data = datasets[[name]],
      name = name,
      is_first = is_first,
      is_last = is_last
    )

    plots[[i]] <- result_single_histogram[[1]]
    list_of_category_percentages[[i]] <- result_single_histogram[[2]]
  }

  # Combine plots with patchwork
  combined_plot <- plots[[1]]
  for (i in 2:length(plots)) {
    combined_plot <- combined_plot / plots[[i]]
  }

  # Add overall title and formatting
  final_plot <- combined_plot +
    plot_layout(heights = rep(1, length(plots))) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Energy Burden Comparison: EDC vs MLP",
      subtitle = glue::glue("Medium HP Efficiency | {supply_year} | 100% LI Discount Participation"),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12)
      )
    ) &
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90")
    )

  return(list(final_plot, list_of_category_percentages))
}
```

```{r}
# Load inflation factors
#inflation_factors <- readRDS("/workspaces/reports/data/fred/inflation_factors.rds")


# Load supply rates
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), path_rs_db)
inflation_factors <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "inflation_factors")
supply_rates_elec <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "supply_rates_elec")
supply_rates_gas <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "supply_rates_gas")
supply_rates_fueloil <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "supply_rates_fueloil")
supply_rates_propane <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "supply_rates_propane")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# --------------------------
# Electric
electric_utilities = c("eversource", "nationalgrid", "unitil")
weights = c(0.455, 0.431, 0.008)
weights = weights / sum(weights)

# Create tibble of utility weights
utility_weights <- tibble(
  electric_utility = electric_utilities,
  weight_edc = weights
)


# Create time series plot of supply rates by utility
supply_rates_elec_weighted_inflated <- supply_rates_elec |>
  filter(electric_utility %in% electric_utilities) |>
  left_join(utility_weights, by = "electric_utility") |>
  left_join(inflation_factors, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01")),
    supply_rate_weighted_inflated = supply_rate * weight_edc * inflation_factor
  ) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(supply_rate = sum(supply_rate_weighted_inflated), inflation_factor = mean(inflation_factor), weight_edc = mean(weight_edc))


# --------------------------
# Gas
gas_utilities = c("nationalgrid", "eversource", "liberty", "berkshire", "unitil")
weights_gas = c(0.268, 0.221, 0.002, 0.015, 0.005)
weights_gas = weights_gas / sum(weights_gas)

# Create tibble of utility weights
utility_weights_gas <- tibble(
  gas_utility = gas_utilities,
  weight_edc = weights_gas
)

supply_rates_gas_weighted_inflated <- supply_rates_gas |>
  filter(gas_utility %in% gas_utilities) |>
  left_join(utility_weights_gas, by = "gas_utility") |>
  left_join(inflation_factors, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01")),
    supply_rate_weighted_inflated = supply_rate * weight_edc * inflation_factor
  ) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(supply_rate = sum(supply_rate_weighted_inflated), inflation_factor = mean(inflation_factor), weight_edc = mean(weight_edc))


# --------------------------
# Fuel Oil
# Create tibble of utility weights

supply_rates_fueloil_weighted_inflated <- supply_rates_fueloil |>
  left_join(inflation_factors, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01")),
    supply_rate_weighted_inflated = fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh * inflation_factor
  ) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(supply_rate = sum(supply_rate_weighted_inflated), inflation_factor = mean(inflation_factor))
```
