## Supply Year Sensitivity
```{r}
#| label: fig-supply-year-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "The relative price of electric energy to natural gas drives the bill impacts of switching to heat pumps."

path_annual_change_db = "/workspaces/reports/data/ma_hp_rates/annual_change.db"

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), path_annual_change_db)
annual_change_with_municipal <- DBI::dbReadTable(con, "annual_change_with_municipal")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

categorize_bill_changes_by_utility <- function(data) {
  data |>
    filter(bill_type == "annual_bill_change_energy",
           hvac == hvac_for_utility_bills,
           version_elec %in% c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")) |>
    mutate(category = case_when(
      annual_bill_change <= -1000 ~ "large_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 0 ~ "small_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 1000 ~ "small_increase",
      TRUE ~ "large_increase"
    )) |>
    group_by(version_elec, category, year) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(version_elec, year) |>
    mutate(
      total = sum(count),
      percentage = count / total * 100,
      utility_scenario = paste(version_elec, year, sep = "_")
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}


# Apply the function to the data
supply_year_scenario_bins <- categorize_bill_changes_by_utility(annual_change_with_municipal)

# Set factor levels for correct ordering
supply_year_scenario_bins <- supply_year_scenario_bins |>
  mutate(
    # FIXED: Order for stacking - this controls the visual stacking order
    # For negative values, the order is visually reversed, so we put large_savings before small_savings
    category = factor(
      category,
      levels = c("large_increase", "small_increase", "large_savings", "small_savings")
    ),
    version_elec = factor(
      version_elec,
      levels = c("baseline", "hpr_approved", "hpr_doer")
    ),
    year = factor(
      year,
      levels = c("2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024")
    )
  )

col_width = 0.8

# Create a single faceted plot showing all three scenarios
faceted_plot <- ggplot(supply_year_scenario_bins, aes(x = year, y = percentage, fill = category)) +
  # Reference line at 0 (boundary between savings and increases)
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Stacked bars for increases (positive values)
  geom_col(
    data = supply_year_scenario_bins |> filter(category %in% c("small_increase", "large_increase")),
    aes(y = percentage),
    position = "stack",
    width = col_width
    ) +
  # Stacked bars for savings (negative values)
  geom_col(
    data = supply_year_scenario_bins |> filter(category %in% c("small_savings", "large_savings")),
    aes(y = -percentage),
    position = "stack",
    width = col_width
    ) +
  # Add percentage labels for savings (negative values)
  geom_text(
    data = supply_year_scenario_bins |> filter(category %in% c("large_savings", "small_savings")),
    aes(y = -percentage, label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  # Add percentage labels for increases (positive values)
  geom_text(
    data = supply_year_scenario_bins |> filter(category %in% c("small_increase", "large_increase")),
    aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  # Facet by version_elec to create separate panels
  facet_wrap(~ version_elec,
             labeller = labeller(version_elec = c(
               "baseline" = "Baseline Rates",
               "hpr_approved" = "HPR Approved Rates",
               "hpr_doer" = "HPR DOER Rates"
             ))) +
  # Color scheme for categories
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "large_increase" = "#db8b87",     # dark red (top)
      "small_increase" = "#eaada9",     # light red
      "small_savings" = "#8ebd85",      # light green
      "large_savings" = "#5e8a5e"       # dark green (bottom)
    ),
    labels = c(
      "large_increase" = ">$1,000 increase",
      "small_increase" = "$0-$1,000 increase",
      "small_savings" = "$0-$1,000 savings",
      "large_savings" = ">$1,000 savings"
    ),
    breaks = c("large_increase", "small_increase", "small_savings", "large_savings")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "%")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    #name = "Supply Year",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Heating Bill Changes by Supply Year and Rate Scenario",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Bill Change Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.3, "lines")  # Reduce spacing between facet panels
  )

faceted_plot
```

## prototype for fig-hists-revenue-impact
```{r}
#| label: fig-hists-revenue-impact-prototype
#| fig-cap: "The revenue impact of the HPR approved rates and HPR DOER rates."

hist_for_single_rate_version <- function(
  annual_change_table,
  bill_type,
  baseline_heating_type_option,
  hvac,
  appliances,
  shell,
  version_elec,
  x_limits = c(-3000, 3000),
  y_limits = c(0, 100),
  y_step = 10,
  binwidth = 100,
  show_category_labels = TRUE
) {

  # --------------------------------------
  # Plot parameters
  x_min <- x_limits[1]
  x_max <- x_limits[2]

  # Define the breaks for binning
  breaks <- seq(floor(x_min/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(x_max/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)

  # More balanced color palette with less contrast
  dark_red <- "#db8b87"        # dark red
  light_red <- "#eaada9"       # light red
  light_green <- "#8ebd85"     # light green
  dark_green <- "#5e8a5e"      # dark green
  # --------------------------------------

  # Filter data for mid_hp
  plot_data <- annual_change_table |>
    filter(hvac == !!hvac, appliances == !!appliances, shell == !!shell, version_elec == !!version_elec) |>
    filter(bill_type == !!bill_type) |>
    filter(if (baseline_heating_type_option != "All Fuels") baseline_heating_type == !!baseline_heating_type_option else TRUE) |>
    # Add category column before binning with new cutoffs
    mutate(bill_category = case_when(
      annual_bill_change <= -1000 ~ "large_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 0 ~ "small_savings",
      annual_bill_change < 1000 ~ "small_increase",
      TRUE ~ "large_increase"
    ))

  # Calculate percentages for each category
  category_percentages <- plot_data |>
    group_by(bill_category) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(percentage = count / sum(count) * 100)

  # Get percentages for annotation
  pct_large_savings <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "large_savings") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_large_savings) == 0) pct_large_savings <- 0

  pct_small_savings <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "small_savings") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_small_savings) == 0) pct_small_savings <- 0

  pct_that_save <- pct_large_savings + pct_small_savings

  pct_small_increase <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "small_increase") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_small_increase) == 0) pct_small_increase <- 0

  pct_large_increase <- category_percentages |>
    filter(bill_category == "large_increase") |>
    pull(percentage) |>
    round(1)
  if(length(pct_large_increase) == 0) pct_large_increase <- 0

  pct_that_lose <- pct_small_increase + pct_large_increase

  # Manually bin the data and calculate counts - this preserves the bill_category
  binned_data <- plot_data |>
    mutate(bin = cut(annual_bill_change,
                     breaks = breaks,
                     include.lowest = TRUE,
                     right = FALSE)) |>
    group_by(bin, bill_category) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    # Add bin midpoint for plotting
    mutate(bin_mid = as.numeric(as.character(
      sapply(bin, function(b) {
        # Extract bin boundaries and calculate midpoint
        vals <- as.numeric(gsub("\\(|\\]|\\[|\\)", "", strsplit(as.character(b), ",")[[1]]))
        return(mean(vals))
      })
    )))

  # Position the bars at the very top and text just below
  bar_y_pos <- y_limits[2]  # Exactly at the top
  text_y_pos <- y_limits[2] * 0.95  # Just below the colored line

  # Calculate x positions for percentage labels (center of each category)
  x_large_savings <- mean(c(x_min, -1000))
  x_small_savings <- mean(c(-1000, 0))
  x_that_save <- x_min * 0.7
  x_small_increase <- mean(c(0, 1000))
  x_large_increase <- mean(c(1000, x_max))
  x_that_lose <- x_max * 0.7

  # Create the plot using geom_col() with binned data
  px_hist_by_rate_version <- ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = bin_mid, y = count, fill = bill_category)) +
    # Add vertical dotted lines at the category boundaries
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1000, 0, 1000), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", size = 0.5) +

    # Add the bars
    geom_col(position = "stack", width = binwidth * 0.9) +

    # Set the fill colors manually with expanded categories
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "large_savings" = "#5e8a5e",      # dark green
        "small_savings" = "#8ebd85",      # light green
        "small_increase" = "#eaada9",     # light red
        "large_increase" = "#db8b87"      # dark red
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +

    # Add horizontal lines at the very top of the plot
    # With colors matching their respective categories
    annotate("segment",
             x = x_min, xend = -1000,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = dark_green, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = -1000, xend = 0,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = light_green, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = 0, xend = 1000,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = light_red, size = 1) +

    annotate("segment",
             x = 1000, xend = x_max,
             y = bar_y_pos, yend = bar_y_pos,
             color = dark_red, size = 1) +

    # Add percentage labels for each category directly below the lines
    annotate("text",
             x = x_large_savings,
             y = text_y_pos,
             label = paste0(pct_large_savings, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_small_savings,
             y = text_y_pos,
             label = paste0(pct_small_savings, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_small_increase,
             y = text_y_pos,
             label = paste0(pct_small_increase, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_large_increase,
             y = text_y_pos,
             label = paste0(pct_large_increase, "%"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    # Add the percentage labels for the "that save" and "that lose" categories
    annotate("text",
             x = x_that_save,
             y = text_y_pos*0.8,
             label = paste0(pct_that_save, "% pay lower electric bills"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    annotate("text",
             x = x_that_lose,
             y = text_y_pos*0.8,
             label = paste0(pct_that_lose, "% pay higher electric bills"),
             size = 3,
             fontface = "bold") +

    # Rest of the plot styling
    labs(
      title = glue::glue("Change in Total Winter Energy Bills after Switching to Heat Pumps"),
      x = "Annual Bill Change ($)",
      y = "# of Homes"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 1), ""),
      name = "# of Homes",
      limits = y_limits,
      breaks = seq(0, y_limits[2], by=y_step),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::dollar_format(),
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = seq(x_min, x_max, by = 500),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "none",
      aspect.ratio = 0.6,
      margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f2f0eb", color = NA),
      #plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FAFAF5", color = NA)
    ) +
    {
      if (show_category_labels) {
        list(
          annotate("text", x = x_large_savings,   y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "savings > $1k",  size = 3, fontface = "bold"),
          annotate("text", x = x_small_savings,   y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "savings $0–1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold"),  # make bold
          annotate("text", x = x_small_increase,  y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "losses  $0–1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold"),  # make bold
          annotate("text", x = x_large_increase,  y = y_limits[2]*0.97,
                   label = "losses  > $1k", size = 3, fontface = "bold")
        )
      }
    } +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

  return(list(px_hist_by_rate_version, category_percentages))
}



plot_elec_bill_change_histograms <- function(
  annual_change_table,
  bill_type,
  baseline_heating_type_option,
  hvac,
  appliances,
  shell,
  electric_utility_option,
  supply_year,
  second_subtitle = NULL,
  x_limits = c(-2500, 2500),
  y_limits = c(0, 100),
  y_step = 10,
  binwidth = 100
) {


  # Create nicer version labels
  version_labels <- c(
    "baseline" = "     Default\n     Rates",
    "hpr_approved" = "     1.0\n     Rates",
    "hpr_doer" = "     2.0\n     Rates"
  )

  # Create three histograms without individual titles
  result_baseline <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    bill_type = bill_type,
    baseline_heating_type_option = baseline_heating_type_option,
    hvac = hvac,
    appliances = appliances,
    shell = shell,
    version_elec = "baseline",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    y_step = y_step,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p1_baseline <- result_baseline[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +                 # Remove y-axis label
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x axis title from top two plots
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x tick labels from top two plots
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x ticks from top two plots
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 0, 5),  # Consistent margins (top, right, bottom, left)
      axis.title.y = element_blank()     # Remove y title from top plot
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = Inf,  # Use Inf to position at the right edge of the plot
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["baseline"],
             hjust = 0,  # Align to the right edge
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "black",
             vjust = 0.5)  # Center text vertically

  result_approved <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    bill_type = bill_type,
    baseline_heating_type_option = baseline_heating_type_option,
    hvac = hvac,
    appliances = appliances,
    shell = shell,
    version_elec = "hpr_approved",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    y_step = y_step,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p2_approved <- result_approved[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x axis title from top two plots
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),   # Remove x tick labels from top two plots
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x ticks from top two plots
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),   # Remove y title from middle plot
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 0, 5)  # Consistent margins (no top/bottom margin)
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = Inf,  # Use Inf to position at the right edge of the plot
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["hpr_approved"],
             hjust = 0,  # Align to the right edge
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "black",
             vjust = 0.5)  # Center text vertically

  result_doer <- hist_for_single_rate_version(
    annual_change_table = annual_change_table,
    bill_type = bill_type,
    baseline_heating_type_option = baseline_heating_type_option,
    hvac = hvac,
    appliances = appliances,
    shell = shell,
    version_elec = "hpr_doer",
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    y_step = y_step,
    binwidth = binwidth,
    show_category_labels = FALSE
  )

  p3_doer <- result_doer[[1]] +
    labs(title = NULL) +  # Remove title
    ylab(NULL) +
    theme(
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),  # Remove y title from bottom plot
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 5, 5),  # Consistent margins
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
    ) +
    # Add elegant version label on right side
    annotate("text",
             x = Inf,  # Use Inf to position at the right edge of the plot
             y = y_limits[2] * 0.7,
             label = version_labels["hpr_doer"],
             hjust = 0,  # Align to the right edge
             fontface = "bold",
             size = 4,
             color = "black",
             vjust = 0.5)  # Center text vertically

  # Combine plots with shared x and y axes
  combined_plot <- p1_baseline / p2_approved / p3_doer +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1)) +  # Equal heights for all plots
    plot_annotation(
      title = case_when(
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_elec" ~ glue::glue("Switching from {baseline_heating_type_option} to Heat Pump: Change in Annual Electric Bill"),
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_energy" ~ glue::glue("Change in Total Winter Energy Bills after Switching to Heat Pump from {baseline_heating_type_option}"),
        bill_type == "annual_bill_change_gas" ~ glue::glue("Switching from {baseline_heating_type_option} to Heat Pump: Change in Annual Gas Bill"),
        TRUE ~ "Heat Pump Rate Bill Changes" # Default case
      ),
      subtitle = second_subtitle,
      theme = theme(
        plot.margin = margin(1,1,5,1),  # top, right, bottom, left
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
      )
    ) &
    # Apply consistent theming to all plots
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "gray90"),
      aspect.ratio = 0.18,
      plot.margin = margin(1,25,8,1),  # top, right, bottom, left
    )

  # Wrap the combined plot to add a shared y-axis label
  combined_plot <- patchwork::wrap_elements(combined_plot) +
    labs(tag = "# of Homes") +
    theme(
      plot.tag = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, face = "plain", size = 9),
      plot.tag.position = "left"
    )

  return(list(combined_plot, result_baseline[[2]], result_approved[[2]], result_doer[[2]]))
}
```


## Revenue Impact estimate - just volumetric
```{r}
#| label: data-hist-delivery-revenue-volumetric-estimate
#| fig-cap: "The electric delivery revenue impact of the HPR approved rates and HPR DOER rates."

default_delivery_rate_eversource = 0.19122
hpr1_delivery_rate_eversource = 0.12094
hpr2_delivery_rate_eversource = 0.0702

default_delivery_rate_nationalgrid = 0.18091
hpr1_delivery_rate_nationalgrid = 0.12669
hpr2_delivery_rate_nationalgrid = 0.06652

default_delivery_rate_unitil = 0.26493
hpr1_delivery_rate_unitil = 0.20307
hpr2_delivery_rate_unitil = 0.09652



elec_revenue_currrent_hvac <- winter_energy |>
  filter(hvac == "current") |>
  filter(fuel == "electricity") |>
  select(bldg_id, hvac, total_winter_kwh, electric_utility) |>
  mutate(
    elec_revenue_default_current =  case_when(
      electric_utility == "unitil" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_unitil,
      electric_utility == "nationalgrid" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_nationalgrid,
      electric_utility == "eversource" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_eversource,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("elec_revenue_"),
    names_to = "version_elec",
    values_to = "elec_revenue"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    version_elec = case_when(
      version_elec == "elec_revenue_default_current" ~ "baseline"
    )
  ) |>
  select(bldg_id, hvac, total_winter_kwh, version_elec, elec_revenue, electric_utility)


elec_revenue_mid_hp <- winter_energy |>
  filter(hvac == "mid_hp") |>
  filter(fuel == "electricity") |>
  select(bldg_id, hvac, total_winter_kwh, electric_utility) |>
  mutate(
    elec_revenue_default_mid_hp = case_when(
      electric_utility == "unitil" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_unitil,
      electric_utility == "nationalgrid" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_nationalgrid,
      electric_utility == "eversource" ~ total_winter_kwh * default_delivery_rate_eversource,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    elec_revenue_hpr1_mid_hp = case_when(
      electric_utility == "unitil" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr1_delivery_rate_unitil,
      electric_utility == "nationalgrid" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr1_delivery_rate_nationalgrid,
      electric_utility == "eversource" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr1_delivery_rate_eversource,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    elec_revenue_hpr2_mid_hp = case_when(
      electric_utility == "unitil" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr2_delivery_rate_unitil,
      electric_utility == "nationalgrid" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr2_delivery_rate_nationalgrid,
      electric_utility == "eversource" ~ total_winter_kwh * hpr2_delivery_rate_eversource,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("elec_revenue_"),
    names_to = "version_elec",
    values_to = "elec_revenue"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    version_elec = case_when(
      version_elec == "elec_revenue_default_mid_hp" ~ "baseline",
      version_elec == "elec_revenue_hpr1_mid_hp" ~ "hpr_approved",
      version_elec == "elec_revenue_hpr2_mid_hp" ~ "hpr_doer"
    )
  ) |>
  select(bldg_id, hvac, total_winter_kwh, version_elec, elec_revenue, electric_utility)

elec_revenue <- elec_revenue_mid_hp |>
  bind_rows(elec_revenue_currrent_hvac) |>
  select(bldg_id, hvac, version_elec, total_winter_kwh, elec_revenue, electric_utility) |>
  left_join(housing_units |> select(bldg_id, in.sqft, electric_utility, gas_utility, assigned_income, building_type_group, baseline_heating_type), by = c("bldg_id","electric_utility")) |>
  mutate(
    shell = "current",
    appliances = "current",
    bill_type = "annual_delivery_revenue_elec"
  )

rm(elec_revenue_currrent_hvac, elec_revenue_mid_hp)

elec_revenue_change <- elec_revenue |>
  # Get the baseline revenue for each building
  left_join(
    elec_revenue |>
      filter(hvac == "current", version_elec == "baseline") |>
      select(bldg_id, baseline_revenue = elec_revenue, baseline_total_winter_kwh = total_winter_kwh, electric_utility),
    by = c("bldg_id", "electric_utility")
  ) |>
  # Calculate the change in revenue
  mutate(
    bill_type = "annual_delivery_revenue_change_elec",
    annual_kwh_change = total_winter_kwh - baseline_total_winter_kwh,
    annual_bill_change = elec_revenue - baseline_revenue
  ) |>
  select(-baseline_revenue)
```

```{r}
#| label: stats-annual-elec-revenue-change
# Stats
calc_elec_revenue_stats_by_rate_version <- function(annual_change_table, hp_eff_for_stats, print_table = FALSE) {
  scenario_stats <- annual_change_table |>
    filter(hvac == hp_eff_for_stats) |>
    filter(!is.na(annual_bill_change)) |>  # Remove NA values
    group_by(version_elec) |>
    summarise(
      # kWh change
      median_kwh_change = median(annual_kwh_change),

      # Bill change
      median_bill_change = median(annual_bill_change),
      pct_that_save = mean(annual_bill_change < 0) * 100,
      pct_that_save_big = mean(annual_bill_change < -1000) * 100,
      pct_that_lose = mean(annual_bill_change > 0) * 100,
      pct_that_lose_big = mean(annual_bill_change > 1000) * 100,
      median_bill_savings = median(annual_bill_change[annual_bill_change < 0]),
      median_bill_loss = median(annual_bill_change[annual_bill_change > 0])
    )

  if (print_table) {
    print(knitr::kable(scenario_stats,
               caption = glue::glue("Summary Statistics by Rate Version (HP Efficiency = {hp_eff_for_stats})"),
               format = "pipe",
               digits = 1,
               col.names = c("Rate Version", "Median Bill Change ($)", "% That Save", "Median Savings ($)", "Median Loss ($)")))
  }

  return(scenario_stats)
}

scenario_stats_elec_types_mid_hp <- calc_elec_revenue_stats_by_rate_version(elec_revenue_change, hp_eff_for_stats = "mid_hp", print_table = FALSE)

fig_hists_delivery_revenue_baseline_pct_that_lose <- scenario_stats_elec_types_mid_hp |> filter(version_elec == "baseline") |> pull(pct_that_lose)

# HPR 2.0
fig_hists_delivery_revenue_hpr2_median_bill_change <- scenario_stats_elec_types_mid_hp |> filter(version_elec == "hpr_doer") |> pull(median_bill_change)
fig_hists_delivery_revenue_hpr2_median_kwh_change <- scenario_stats_elec_types_mid_hp |> filter(version_elec == "hpr_doer") |> pull(median_kwh_change)
```

```{r}
revenue_hists <- plot_elec_bill_change_histograms(

  baseline_heating_type_option = "All Fuels",

  second_subtitle = "Change in Winter Electric Delivery Bills (Volumetric Component Only)",
  x_limits = c(-3000, 3000),
  y_limits = c(0, 3000),
  y_step = 500,
  binwidth = 250
)

print(revenue_hists[[1]])
```
